primitives.note: Rocket Jump's landing damage and Buster Shot's impact damage are single damage instances that land after a cast/landing delay, then go on cooldown
Rapid Fire grants a flat bonus-attack-speed buff for a fixed 7s duration on cast; it is non-refreshing and does not update on rank-up
Explosive Charge accrues 0-4 stacks on the attached target from basic attacks (on-hit) and ability hits, each stack adding 25% to the eventual detonation damage; reaching 4 forces instant detonation

Explosive Charge is applied on cast (0 damage) and detonates later (on stack cap, 4s expiry, or delayed to the end of a Buster Shot knockback), making the toss and the detonation two separately timed damage-relevant events
Explosive Charge's detonation total damage is multiplicatively scaled by crit chance x (crit damage - 1) via CritChanceModifier, independent of whether the ability itself can crit
Rocket Jump's cooldown resets on an enemy champion takedown or on detonating a maxed Explosive Charge on a champion
Explosive Charge's passive AoE explosion only triggers when a basic attack kills the target
Mana costs on all four abilities (notably Buster Shot's flat 100) can meaningfully cap how many casts fit in a 15s fight depending on mana pool

needsBespoke.why: The kit's centerpiece mechanic (Explosive Charge's stack-building, capped amplification, delayed/conditional detonation, and crit-chance-based total-damage scaling) is expressible as a combination of target-stacks, recast-or-multipart and crit-interaction primitives rather than requiring new logic. The remaining pieces (W and R as plain-cast damage, Q as a timed self-buff, W's cooldown reset) also map cleanly onto existing primitives.

unsettled.question: Does the initial toss of Explosive Charge (which deals 0 damage) count as one of the 4 stacks needed for instant detonation, or do all 4 stacks have to come from subsequent attacks/ability hits after the toss lands?
options: The toss itself contributes no stack; 4 further hits (attacks or abilities) are needed to hit the cap and detonate instantly
The toss counts as an implicit first application and only 3 more hits are needed
Sources do not distinguish and this must be tested
quotes: Tristana's basic attacks on-hit and abilities against the target increase Explosive Charge's damage by {{ap|{{#var:e_a_s}}*100}}%, stacking up to 4 times for a maximum {{ap|{{#var:e_a_s}}*400}}% increase, upon which the charge also detonates instantly.

unsettled.question: Does casting Rapid Fire (Q) again while its 7s attack-speed buff is still active refresh/extend the buff, get wasted, or run as an independent second instance?
options: Recast refreshes the timer to a fresh 7s
Recast is effectively wasted since the non-refreshing buff cannot be reapplied while active
Recast creates a separate stacking or overlapping instance
quotes: ''Rapid Fire'' is a non-refreshing buff that will not update on rank-up.

unsettled.question: The automatic basic attack Tristana is 'ordered to' perform after Explosive Charge's cast time and after Buster Shot's cast — is this a bonus attack equivalent to an attack-reset (extra swing beyond normal attack timer), or does it simply consume/replace whatever the next regular queued auto-attack would have been (no net DPS gain)?
options: It is a guaranteed extra swing on top of the normal attack timer (acts like an attack-reset)
It merely fires the next regular auto-attack early/on schedule with no bonus swing added
quotes: '''Tristana''' will be automatically ordered to basic attack the target after the cast time.
'''Tristana''' will attempt to basic attack the target afterwards.

unsettled.question: Explosive Charge's cast time equals 100% of Tristana's current attack windup and therefore changes dynamically with attack speed (from Rapid Fire, items, level). Should the simulator recompute this cast time live from current total attack speed at the moment of each E cast, or use a fixed base-AS value throughout the fight?
options: Recompute dynamically each cast from current total attack speed (post Q buff/items)
Use the fixed base-attack-speed cast time (0.225625s) for all casts for simplicity
quotes: ''Explosive Charge's'' cast time is always 100% of the caster's attack windup time.
An easy formula to calculate the cast time is [ {{fd|0.14801}} seconds divided by {{as|'''total''' attack speed|attack speed}} ].

proposal: Pre-cast Explosive Charge (E) on the dummy immediately to start the stack/duration clock as early as possible.
Cast Rocket Jump (W) onto or next to the dummy for its landing magic damage.
Cast Rapid Fire (Q) right after to gain the attack-speed buff for the bulk of the fight.
Auto-attack continuously; each auto-attack on the charged target both deals normal damage and adds an Explosive Charge stack.
Cast Buster Shot (R) as soon as it is off cooldown for its large magic burst, ideally timed as the follow-up ability hit that helps push Explosive Charge to max stacks.
Recast Explosive Charge every time it comes off cooldown, weaving autos in to build it to 4 stacks (instant detonation) before its 4s attach duration lapses if possible.
Recast Rocket Jump on its normal cooldown (and again immediately if a max-stack Explosive Charge detonation on the dummy or the dummy's death resets it).
Recast Rapid Fire as soon as it is off cooldown to keep the attack-speed buff up as much as possible.
Fill all remaining time with continuous auto-attacks between ability cooldowns.
questions: Against a single stationary already-in-range dummy, is Rocket Jump's dash distance/positioning irrelevant, and does its landing damage still register normally without any real repositioning need?
Should Explosive Charge be recast on cooldown regardless of whether the prior charge has detonated yet, or does a charge already active on the target block a new cast until it resolves?

Is Buster Shot's automatic post-cast basic attack and Explosive Charge's automatic post-cast basic attack additive with the normal attack queue, i.e., can they be relied on as 'free' extra stacks/damage in the rotation?
Does mana realistically run out for Tristana within the 15s window at the tested level/item state, given Q/W/E/R's combined costs, forcing skipped casts?
